correctness.rationale: Greedy arch lemma is proved; parity on fixed-letter counts gives the exact qk versus qk+f−1 lower bound; equality forces the central fixed occurrence to be the middle of the 2r+1 disjoint complete blocks. Minimal left/right arch lengths plus central orbit coverage force r full permutation blocks and an exact orbit transversal. Constructing these provides sufficiency and injective factorial counting. The independent stdlib verifier checks 1,385,969 symmetric words, 7,632 classified extremizers and 79,828 full-pattern comparisons across 34 configurations; finite tests only supplement, not replace, the proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The general existence and algorithm results do not assert or supply a stronger parameterized extremal theorem for arbitrary mixed involutions. Proposition 18 permits symbol permutations but does not directly force a central transversal or the f−1 penalty. The proof supplies an independent optimization under a nontrivial global antimorphic constraint.

evidence: Barker’s pure palindrome midpoint relation addresses identity-involution only, with all letters fixed.
The fixed-point-free endpoint has the reverse-complement center-pair phenomenon and lacks the fixed-symbol parity surplus; it does not directly yield f−1 for f>=1.
The new construction uses exactly one representative from each swapped pair and all noncentral fixed letters.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The conclusion is not a corollary merely from ordinary universal-word length qk or the identity/pair-only cases. Its odd formula depends on q=2p+f with p,f both positive, and necessity is derived by matching left and right arch boundaries and central letter counts. Pure endpoints are not claimed.

evidence: arXiv:2003.04629v1 Proposition 15 treats ordinary reversal; mixed symbols create fixed-point parity obligations not present in that result.
arXiv:2304.04583v1 counts unconstrained words rather than mixed antimorphism fixed words.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The symmetry condition is a fixed-point equation under reverse followed by a nontrivial involution with fixed letters and transpositions. It cannot be conjugated by a relabeling into either ordinary reversal or fixed-point-free complement because orbit type is invariant. Known endpoint formulas therefore do not yield the exact mixed optimal length and witness count without new structural argument.

evidence: Barker et al. 2020 provides qualitative arch characterization and ordinary-palindrome index comparison, no listed mixed (p,f) counts.
Direct enumeration outputs are original diagnostics of the present theorem, not a claim that short sequence values themselves are new.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The result is a proof for all k,p,f rather than an unmotivated finite table. Searches did not find an existing mixed orbit-profile table/formula that would subsume it. Lack of indexing alone is not relied on for uniqueness.

originality.rationale: A result for every mixed orbit profile (p>=1 transpositions and f>=1 fixed letters) establishes a new parity penalty f-1, exact orbit-transversal structural characterization and factorial count. The closest arXiv primary texts were materially examined: standard arch, all-fixed palindrome and unrestricted enumeration results do not directly imply the mixed formulas. The pure endpoint cases are expressly credited. Searches and accessible statement comparisons found no exact claim; this is a qualified best-knowledge originality judgment, not a proof of global priority.
residual_risks: An equivalent mixed-involution theorem might exist in unindexed combinatorics-on-words literature or non-English material.
The contextual DNA-coding article was not used to assert full-text noncoverage; only its public abstract/metadata was inspected.

value.rationale: The mixed fixed-point and swapped-pair case is the natural previously missing orbit type between palindrome and reverse-complement universality. The theorem supplies an all-k, all-orbit-profiles optimal length, complete set of minimizers and exact number of minimizing labeled words, with a sharp f-dependent penalty rather than a local finite table. This gives exact constructive templates for reversible-symmetry constrained scattered-subsequence coverage.
